description: The bar chart illustrates the execution accuracy of two Text-to-SQL models, NatSQL (light blue) and TA-SQL (dark blue), across three query difficulty levels — Simple, Moderate, and Challenging — as well as an overall Total score. The vertical axis, labeled “Execution Accuracy,” ranges from 20 to 60 with tick marks at intervals of 10, representing percentage points. For Simple queries, NatSQL achieves 60.21% accuracy while TA-SQL reaches 63.14%. In Moderate queries, NatSQL scores 39.64% compared to TA-SQL’s 48.60%. For Challenging queries, NatSQL’s accuracy drops to 32.32%, while TA-SQL performs slightly better at 36.11%. The Total execution accuracy across all query types is 51.35% for NatSQL and 56.19% for TA-SQL. Across all categories, TA-SQL consistently outperforms NatSQL, with the largest gap observed in Moderate queries (8.96 percentage points) and the smallest in Challenging queries (3.79 percentage points). The bars are grouped by query type, with NatSQL always positioned to the left of TA-SQL within each group, and each bar is labeled with its exact accuracy value. The chart visually emphasizes TA-SQL’s superior performance across all difficulty levels, supporting the paper’s claim that its alignment strategy effectively mitigates hallucinations in SQL generation.
